```python
import pytest

from your_module import slugify


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_text", "expected"),
    [
        ("Hello World", "hello-world"),
        ("HELLO WORLD", "hello-world"),
        ("hello", "hello"),
        ("", ""),
        ("hello  world", "hello--world"),
        (" hello world ", "-hello-world-"),
        ("Hello, World!", "hello,-world!"),
        ("123 ABC", "123-abc"),
    ],
)
def test_slugify(input_text, expected):
    assert slugify(input_text) == expected
```

Replace `your_module` with the name of the Python file containing `slugify`, without the `.py` extension. These tests reflect the function’s exact behavior: it lowercases text and replaces each literal space with `-`; it does not normalize punctuation or collapse repeated spaces.
